title: Agent roles per generation step
body:
## Context

The user's "next big change": every generation step from the stakeholder input down to the implementation gets an agent role, so a step no longer needs the full context of all document levels. v0.8.0 prepared it: every level skill names what it reads (`## Reads`), and the review gates stop between the levels.

## Idea

- One role per level: requirements (SPEC → FR/NFR), acceptance (FR → AT), architecture (check, LF, ADR), technical specification (FR/NFR → TS), stories (TS → US), implementation (US → code and tests).
- A role gets only what its skill's `Reads` names, plus the items it works on.
- The hand-over between roles is the review gate: the output of one level, reviewed, is the input of the next.

## Open Questions

- Where are roles defined: in the skills, in a separate role file, or in the project's `AGENTS.md`?
- How does a role refuse work outside its level (e.g. a TS role that finds a missing requirement)? Today `update-requirement` stops after the impact report; the role would hand back the same way.
- Does a role need a model or effort hint, or is that the harness's business?

## Done When

- Every level skill names its role and its hand-over.
- The README user's guide shows a feature going through the roles.
- Tried end to end in one project (wos-intel or project-template).

title: Reverse traceability rule: every item of a kind is referenced
body:
## Context

Traceability rules check "every X references a Y". The architecture overview needs the other direction: every functional requirement is served by at least one logical function (`LF-n` references `FR-x.y`). spec-system says the validator does not check it yet; `update-architecture` checks it by hand.

## Idea

A rule form for "every Y is referenced by an X", e.g. `{"kind": "FR", "referencedBy": ["LF"], "name": "function"}`, reported like the existing rules (`FR-2.1 is served by no function`). Off unless configured.

## Done When

- The rule is in the config schema, the FR and the tests of spec-validator.
- Released; the release notes name the rule.

title: Use the reverse traceability rule for the architecture coverage check
body:
## Context

Once spec-validator has the reverse rule (AS-2), the coverage check "every FR is served by a function" can move from `update-architecture` into the validator.

## Done When

- spec-system "Architecture Overview / Validation" lists the rule; the sentence "does not yet check" is gone.
- `architecture-adopt` adds the rule to `.spec-validator.json`; `update-architecture` relies on the validator instead of checking by hand.
- The tag message names the change under "Affects projects" (raise the lock, add the rule).

title: Durations in the test report
body:
## Context

Since agent-skills v0.8.0 every test run records the execution time of every test. The BDT test report (`-test-report`, Cucumber JSON → AsciiDoc) doesn't show them yet, although the Cucumber JSON holds a duration per step (nanoseconds).

## Idea

The report shows the duration per scenario (sum of its steps) and the total; optionally the slowest scenarios at the top.

## Done When

- The test report of a release shows the durations; FR and tests updated; released.

title: Manual tests (MT) as a test kind
body:
## Context

Some requirements can only be accepted by hand: in wos-intel, runs against the real device. spec-validator's config already has a list of test kinds, so manual tests were planned from the start of BDT.

## Idea

- An MT item: preconditions, steps, expected results, traced to FR/NFR like an AT.
- A record of each execution (date, version, who, result) that the test report and the traceability report include.

## Open Questions

- Format: Gherkin with a tag, or AsciiDoc items?
- Where does the execution record live, and does a release require a recent one?
- Does spec-validator need changes beyond the test-kind list?

title: Blackbox tests with a fake at the process boundary
body:
## Context

A product that drives an external program or device (wos-intel drives the game through `adb`) has no blackbox scenarios for its main loop: the run needs the device. wos-intel can configure the path of its tool (`device.adb_path`), so a scripted fake executable would allow scenarios for the run loop without a device.

## Idea

`bdt-adopt` (or the testing guidance) describes the pattern: the product stays a separate process; the external program is replaced by a fake executable on the configured path, scripted per scenario. The fake lives with the tests, never in the shipped configuration.

## Done When

- The pattern is described once, language-independent; the profiles show how a fake executable is provided.
- Tried in wos-intel (its own story there).

title: Guidance on test doubles for deterministic collaborators
body:
## Context

wos-intel's run-loop tests were slow because each look of the fake game ran the full detection. Two fixes were weighed (see docs/design-notes.md, "Testing"):

- a cache keyed by the input content: little code, the real collaborator stays in the test;
- mocks plus a contract table checked against the real collaborator: clean layering, more maintenance.

Mocks without a contract can drift from the real behaviour wherever no test checks the mocked value.

## Idea

A short rule in the testing guidance: measure first; for a deterministic, expensive collaborator prefer a content-keyed cache; use mocks only with a contract that is checked against the real thing.

## Done When

- The rule is in one place (toolchain or a test skill), language-independent.

title: Recognise anchors inside table cells
body:
## Context

spec-validator recognises an anchor (`[[ID]]`) only when it stands alone on a line. In a table cell it has to go on its own line, which spec-system now documents. The architecture's function table and allocation matrix hit this.

## Idea

Recognise anchors at the start of an AsciiDoc table cell (`| [[LF-1]] Observe`), or decide that the current rule stays and close this.

## Done When

- Decided; if implemented, the spec-system rule is relaxed in the next library version.

title: Import docs/issues.csv into a GitHub project
body:
## Context

Open ideas are kept in docs/issues.csv until the library uses GitHub issues. Each row holds what an issue needs: repository, type, title, labels, milestone, dependencies and the body.

## Idea

A script that creates the issues with `gh issue create` in the row's repository, adds them to a GitHub project, links `depends_on` as sub-issues or references, and writes the issue URLs back (or prints them), so the CSV can be retired.

## Done When

- All rows exist as issues; the CSV is removed or marked as imported.

title: Offer the architecture overview as a template variant
body:
## Context

Since agent-skills v0.8.0 the architecture overview is opt-in (`architecture-adopt`). project-template's variants cover language and BDT, not the architecture.

## Idea

A further variant dimension (e.g. `init.sh <node|python> <bdt|plain> [arch] <name>`) that runs the result of `architecture-adopt`: `architecture-web.adoc`, the kinds ADR and LF in `.spec-validator.json`, the line in `AGENTS.md`.

## Done When

- The variant is generated and green in the template's CI.

title: Vendor agent-skills v0.8.0 into project-template
body:
## Context

project-template still vendors v0.7.0. v0.8.0 changes the test commands of the profiles (every test run records its durations).

## Done When

- The template vendors v0.8.0; every variant's test task writes its duration report and ignores `build/`; CI green.
- Waits for the user's go.
